![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186166867/plots/96a1b00defb1967c7cf00050b628583790af1e6c99f03d56b560be04e26d36ec.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the right-opening parabola shown above.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola has its vertex at $O,$ and passes through the point $(3,3).$

The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=3$ and $y=3$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(3)^{2} & =4p(3) \\ 9 & =12p \\ p & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=3x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3}{2y}\end{aligned}
$$
